title: Ambiguous evidence: opinions vs facts when evidence is open to interpretation

notes: Each card is individually ambiguous: consistent with the correct answer and at least one wrong answer.
Only combining both cards narrows to one explanation.
Three of four analysts start favoring one wrong explanation.
The only changed variable is whether the shared record contains original evidence only or original evidence plus earlier analyst conclusions.
Primary outcomes: exact group choice, detached-support rate, and required-card source coverage among final supporters.
